result:
I found and fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. I wrote a script that reads each rule's docstring (type, percent, threshold, cap) and builds a reference result from the module's shared rules. It compared all 150 rules over about 3,000 random inputs plus edge cases like the exact threshold and very large values. Before the fix 11 rules differed; after the fix all 150 match.

| Rule | Docstring | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21, 72, 98, 116 | whole | Discount was taken only on units above the threshold (the marginal formula) | `base * pct // 100` |
| 54 | whole 7% | Used `round()`, which rounds the discount instead of flooring it | `base * 7 // 100` |
| 62 | marginal, cap 100,000 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always apply `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 74 | marginal, cap 100,000 | Capped the amount before the discount, not the discount | Compute the discount, then `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 80 | whole, cap 30,000 | Same: capped the amount instead of the discount | Compute the discount, then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 83, 106 | 10% | Code applied 11% | Changed to 10% |
| 92 | 100+ units | Discount started at 101 units (`>= 101`) | Changed to `>= 100` |

Rule 50 is a marginal rule written as `qty > 5` instead of `>= 5`. I left it as is, because at exactly 5 units the marginal discount is 0 either way, so the results are the same.

Only those 11 lines changed. Nothing else in the file, including `RULES` and `quote`, was touched. A backup of the original is at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
